items.q: Why are there no named clients?
items.a: We are a new Ontario company, and no case study is published yet. We publish one only with the client's written approval of its text and figures. A client may stay unnamed; the case then names only its segment and province.

items.q: Can we speak to a client in our segment?
items.a: [reference clients available, number]. Speaking to a client needs one in your segment who agrees in writing. Until then, run the checks above or talk to the engineer who would lead your project.

items.q: Are the figures from your tests or from the client?
items.a: Factory acceptance test (FAT) figures are ours, measured on our feed water. Site acceptance test (SAT) and operational qualification (OQ) figures are measured on the client's site. Performance qualification (PQ) data is the client's, published only with its approval and labelled.

items.q: Does a passed FAT mean the system meets USP?
items.a: No. A factory acceptance test (FAT) proves function before shipment, on our feed water. United States Pharmacopeia (USP) quality at your points of use is proven on your feed water. Performance qualification (PQ) proves it, after site acceptance testing (SAT) and operational qualification (OQ).
